sections.heading: Mexico
sections.body: *¿Qué onda?* (What's up?), *güey / wey* (dude — very informal), *chido* (cool), *padre* (great), *neta* (truth: *¿Neta?* — Really?), *chamba* (job), *lana* (money), *¡Aguas!* (Watch out!), *¡No manches!* (No way! — polite form of a ruder phrase), *ahorita* (in a bit / right now), *fresa* (posh, snobby), *chela* (beer).

sections.heading: Caribbean, Colombia and Venezuela
sections.body: *Chévere* (great), *pana* (buddy — Venezuela, Ecuador), *parce / parcero* (buddy — Colombia), *¿Qué más?* (How's it going? — Colombia), *bacano* (cool — Colombia), *¡Qué vaina!* (What a pain! — Venezuela, Colombia; *vaina* = thing), *guagua* (bus — Cuba, Puerto Rico, Canary Islands; but in Chile *guagua* = baby!), *jevo / jeva* (boyfriend / girlfriend — Puerto Rico, Dominican Republic), *tíguere* (streetwise guy — Dominican Republic).

sections.heading: Southern Cone and Andes
sections.body:
**Argentina/Uruguay:** *che* (hey), *boludo* (dude / idiot — depends on tone!), *laburo* (job), *mina* (woman — colloquial), *re* (very: *re lindo*), *¡Qué quilombo!* (What a mess!), *bárbaro* (great).
**Chile:** *po* (tag after *sí, no, ya*: *Sí, po*), *¿cachai?* (you get it?), *fome* (boring), *pololo / polola* (boyfriend / girlfriend), *pega* (job), *luca* (1,000 pesos).
**Peru:** *pata* (friend), *chamba* (job), *jato* (house), *bacán* (cool), *causa* (buddy).

sections.heading: Using slang wisely
sections.body: Understand it first; use it only with people you know, in the right country. Many words shift meaning across borders — *coger, pisto, concha* and others can be innocent in one country and vulgar in another. When in doubt, stay neutral.

examples: ¡Qué vaina! Se me olvidaron las llaves.
What a pain! I forgot my keys.
Tomamos la guagua para ir a la playa.
We took the bus to go to the beach. (Cuba)
Mañana tengo que ir al laburo temprano.
Tomorrow I have to go to work early. (Argentina)
Mi pata me prestó su carro.
My friend lent me his car. (Peru)
